stories.title: Gencom Makes Its First European Luxury Hotel Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Gencom, a Miami-based investment firm, has acquired Rosewood London, a landmark 308-key luxury hotel situated at 252 High Holborn in Central London. The acquisition for a reported £300 million (approximately US$402 million) represents Gencom’s first luxury hotel asset in Europe. The transaction strengthens Gencom’s long-standing relationship with the Rosewood brand, marking the firm’s second owned Rosewood asset, having previously acquired the Rosewood Bermuda in 2017. HVS Hodges Ward Elliott represented the seller. “Rosewood London has earned its place among the world’s premier luxury hotels, distinguished by its iconic setting in one of the most important global gateway cities and by an exceptional guest experience that continues to resonate with the most discerning travelers,” said Karim Alibhai, founder and principal of Gencom. “This acquisition reflects our strong conviction in the long-term strength, resilience and global appeal of the London hospitality market. It also represents an important milestone in our growing relationship with Rosewood, one of the world’s preeminent ultra-luxury hospitality brands.” The transaction was financed by HSBC and Santander. The post Gencom Makes Its First European Luxury Hotel Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gencom acquires Rosewood London for £300M (~$402M); first European luxury hotel.
308-key asset in Central London; Gencom's second Rosewood property globally.
Transaction signals capital deployment into global gateway hospitality markets.
stories.summary: Miami-based investment firm Gencom closed its first European luxury hotel acquisition, purchasing the 308-key Rosewood London at 252 High Holborn for approximately $402 million. This marks Gencom's second owned Rosewood asset and reflects confidence in London's long-term hospitality market strength. The deal was brokered by HVS Hodges Ward Elliott.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. While it signals capital availability and appetite for trophy real estate in global gateways, hotel acquisitions do not compete for land, labor, or financing in the residential development pipeline. London market dynamics are separate from U.S. multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: Connect CRE Q&A with Towne CEO: Making First and Last Impressions at Properties
stories.excerpt: Founded nearly 40 years ago with a single stand for valet parking, Towne has expanded and evolved its services, its technology and its customer base. At the same time, customers’ requirements and priorities have also evolved. Here, CEO Andrew Kerin discusses how his company assists property owners in making positive impressions as tenants and visitors enter and exit the properties. How would you describe Towne today, and how the company has evolved from parking operator to arrival-to-departure experience parking and mobility partner? Andrew Kerin Towne started nearly 40 years ago with a single valet stand. Our clients’ needs have evolved and so have we. Today, we’re a multi-service parking, hospitality and mobility partner helping owners improve the arrival-to-departure experience, operate more efficiently and grow net operating income (NOI). We’re often responsible for a property’s first and last impressions. Whether that means convenient self-parking or high-touch valet service, those moments shape how people feel about a property and whether they want to return. We bring together experienced people, consistent operations and technology to deliver an exceptional experience while improving performance for owners. Our technology platform, Nexity by Towne, can work alongside our operating services or as a standalone solution. It connects capabilities such as parking access and revenue control, guidance, digital payments, analytics, revenue optimization and valet management, giving owners better visibility into performance. We see parking as more than a transaction. It can strengthen a property’s brand, create revenue and contribute to long-term asset performance. The arrival experience influences how residents, visitors and employees feel about the property, which influences renewal behavior, retention rates and rents. How does Towne work with the CRE industry and what have you learned about what CRE owners need right now? We work with owners across asset class
bullets: Towne evolved from valet parking to arrival-departure experience and mobility partner.
CEO discusses NOI improvement via enhanced tenant/visitor experience and operational efficiency.
Technology platform Nexity by Towne drives performance and property impression management.
stories.summary: Towne, founded 40 years ago as a valet parking operator, has expanded into a multi-service parking, hospitality, and mobility partner. CEO Andrew Kerin describes the company's evolution to help property owners improve the arrival-to-departure experience, operate more efficiently, and grow NOI. The firm's Nexity technology platform enhances operations and visitor experience metrics.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development underwriting or site selection. Towne serves as an ancillary amenity/operator partner; parking and mobility tech can marginally improve NOI but does not signal demand shifts, supply constraints, or cost pressures unique to multifamily.

stories.title: Avison Young Closes on Recapitalization, Setting Stage for Next Phase of Growth
stories.excerpt: Global real estate advisory firm Avison Young today announced the successful closing of its recapitalization, marking an important milestone for the firm and the launch of its next phase of growth. With the transaction complete, Avison Young said it’s moving forward with a solid balance sheet, low debt, recruiting momentum and a growth plan centered on investing in its people, expanding capabilities for clients and pursuing opportunities that strengthen and grow the business. The firm is actively identifying opportunities for both organic expansion and strategic acquisitions in markets, sectors and AI-based technology. “The completion of this recapitalization marks an acceleration point for Avison Young and the beginning of an exciting next chapter,” said Mark E. Rose, chair and CEO. “We have tremendous confidence in where we are going, and our financial partners have demonstrated that they share that confidence by voting with their pocketbooks. Now it is about execution. We are going to be very active, investing in our people, our leading AI technologies and our business, strengthening our services to clients and pursuing opportunities that accelerate our growth.” The firm is implementing its “Avison Young 2031” growth plan, building on its existing strengths while expanding in areas where it sees strong client demand and opportunities to grow. Investments will focus on attracting and developing talent, enhancing client capabilities, investing in its leading technology and expanding the firm’s presence and expertise across key markets and sectors globally. The post Avison Young Closes on Recapitalization, Setting Stage for Next Phase of Growth appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Avison Young closes recapitalization with solid balance sheet and low debt.
Firm launches 'Avison Young 2031' growth plan; pursuing organic expansion and acquisitions.
Investment in AI-based technology, personnel, and market/sector expansion underway.
stories.summary: Global real estate advisory firm Avison Young announced successful closing of its recapitalization, positioning itself with a strong balance sheet and low leverage. The firm is implementing its 'Avison Young 2031' growth plan, which includes investments in people, AI technologies, and strategic acquisitions across markets and sectors to accelerate growth.
stories.impact: Indirect signal of capital flow and advisory capacity in CRE markets. A well-capitalized, growth-focused brokerage may increase competition for deal sourcing and advisory work on multifamily transactions, but does not directly affect development fundamentals, rental demand, or construction feasibility in specific markets.

stories.title: Tech’s Biggest Impact on CRE Will Come from AI (VIDEO)
stories.excerpt: During the recent CREtech New York conference at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, Connect CRE asked industry experts, “What’s one technology you believe will have the biggest impact on CRE over the next five years?” Unsurprisingly, artificial intelligence loomed large on their radar screens. “The one technology that I think is going to have the biggest impact on commercial real estate is definitely agentic workflows,” said Matthew Player, founder and CEO, Zoneomics. He predicted that agentic workflows soon would be able to handle the day-to-day “busy work” as well as more important tasks and free up commercial real estate professionals to focus on value creation and analysis. In the video below, you’ll also hear insights from Rob Teel, CEO of Yardi Systems, and Sharon Wilson Géno, president of the National Multifamily Housing Council. Both cited AI as a driver of change, with Teel also observing how rapidly the technology has evolved. The post Tech’s Biggest Impact on CRE Will Come from AI (VIDEO) appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CREtech New York panelists cite AI and agentic workflows as biggest tech impact.
Zoneomics CEO: AI workflows will automate 'busy work' and free value-creation focus.
Yardi Systems CEO, NMHC president also emphasize AI as driver of sector change.
stories.summary: During CREtech New York, industry experts identified artificial intelligence, particularly agentic workflows, as the technology most likely to transform commercial real estate over the next five years. Experts including Zoneomics' Matthew Player and Yardi's Rob Teel predicted AI would handle routine tasks and free professionals to focus on higher-value analysis and strategy.
stories.impact: Macro trend with long-term operational implications but minimal near-term impact on multifamily supply, demand, capital, or cost. AI adoption may eventually improve underwriting speed, tenant/lease management, and portfolio analytics—marginal efficiency gains—but does not signal shifts in job growth, rents, interest rates, or construction feasibility in specific metros.

stories.title: When Will Rising Interest Rates Impact Pricing? Follow the Contracts.
stories.excerpt: Although Avison Young’s third-quarter 2026 U.S. investment sales report showed a 17.9 percent increase in dollar volume compared with the same period last year, the impact of rising interest rates, including the 10-Year Treasury yield having eclipsed 5 percent on Sept. 15, will take time to register. For multifamily, office, retail, development and industrial, there were $389.3 billion in sales nationwide during the first three quarters of 2026. Based on this, Avison Young is now softening the forecast for the full year to $520 billion, which would still be an increase over last year’s $483 billion, but falls short of this past cycle’s peak in 2021 of $805 billion. Understanding the data. Whenever I speak on the state of the market, I always preface the message by saying how sales reports are rear-view mirror indicators, meaning that by the time a sale is reported in a quarter, it was likely negotiated close to six months before. This is because it can take a month to negotiate the contract and then sign. James Nelson. Photo: Courtesy Avison Young Closing periods are trending for longer as well. Sometimes financing can take 90 to 120 days to secure, and then the deal can be reported and aggregated in the quarter. Thus, rate increases in September may not become evident in the sales figures until the first quarter of next year. Watching contracts. I think the best leading indicator of a sales market is how many contracts are being signed. Although forecasts have tempered sales estimates for the fourth quarter of 2026, I’m happy to report that we are still seeing transactions. Residential does a good job of tracking contracts that are signed. In New York, for example, the Olshan report reports how many luxury residential contracts are signed each month. Most of the residential listings on StreetEasy and through the Real Estate Board of New York are marked in contract close to their signing dates as well. bullets: 10-Year Treasury exceeded 5% on Sept. 15, 2026; impact on pricing lags 6 months.
Avison Young softens full-year 2026 U.S. sales forecast to $520B (vs. $805B peak in 2021).
Contract-to-close window extends 6+ months; financing takes 90–120 days post-contract.
stories.summary: Rising interest rates, including a 10-Year Treasury yield above 5%, will take time to filter into transaction pricing due to the lag between contract negotiation and closing. Avison Young's Q3 2026 U.S. investment sales showed 17.9% dollar volume growth year-over-year, but the firm softened its full-year forecast to $520 billion—above 2025's $483 billion but well below 2021's $805 billion peak. Longer financing and closing timelines compound the lag effect.
stories.impact: Critical for multifamily capital markets and feasibility analysis in late 2026 and beyond. Rising Treasury yields and longer financing windows will pressure underwriting assumptions, cap rates, and loan terms across multifamily development; deals negotiated now reflect pre-rise rates, but closings in Q1–Q2 2027 will price in higher rates. Expect downward pressure on valuations and development returns in H1 2027 as deals close under new rate environment.

stories.title: 1754 Properties Makes First Office Acquisition with Google-Leased San Francisco Asset
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between affiliates of 1754 Properties and Vander Capital Partners has closed on the acquisition of 40 Jessie St., a 49,560-square-foot office building in downtown San Francisco that is 100% leased to Google. The property traded for nearly $28 million, according to the San Francisco Standard. The building has been leased to Google and its predecessor affiliate since 2016. The property combines conventional office space with purpose-built laboratory infrastructure, and the lease runs through December 2030. The acquisition comes amid a broad resurgence in San Francisco’s office market, fueled by the city’s booming AI and technology sectors. According to Cushman & Wakefield, San Francisco recorded 3.6 million square feet of office leasing in the third quarter of 2026, bringing year-to-date new leasing to more than 9.0 million square feet, already exceeding the 12-month 2025 total. “This marks 1754’s first office acquisition, and we look forward to many more,” said Alexander Galewicz, managing partner of 1754 Properties. The post 1754 Properties Makes First Office Acquisition with Google-Leased San Francisco Asset appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 1754 Properties/Vander Capital JV closes on 40 Jessie St., San Francisco; 49,560 SF.
100% Google-leased office building trades for ~$28M; lease runs through Dec 2030.
San Francisco Q3 2026: 3.6M SF office leasing; YTD 9M+ SF, exceeds all of 2025.
stories.summary: A joint venture of 1754 Properties and Vander Capital Partners acquired 40 Jessie Street, a 49,560-square-foot downtown San Francisco office building 100% leased to Google, for approximately $28 million. The lease extends through December 2030. The acquisition reflects a resurgence in San Francisco's office market driven by AI and tech sector growth; the city recorded 3.6 million square feet of office leasing in Q3 2026 alone, with YTD leasing already exceeding the full 2025 total.
stories.impact: Mixed signal for San Francisco multifamily. Strong office leasing and tech expansion bolster employment and in-migration demand for housing, supporting rent growth in central SF and nearby sublets. However, the office market's rebound may compete for institutional capital and development sites in San Francisco's constrained urban core, potentially raising land costs and reducing multifamily development site availability.

stories.title: Related Group Lands $177M to Build Resi Complex at Office Depot HQ
stories.excerpt: Related Group has secured $177.3 million to build a residential complex within Office Depot’s former headquarters in Boca Raton, Fla. The construction financing from Wells Fargo covers a multifamily development featuring 494 luxury apartments and 50 units priced as workforce housing. The bank, serving as an administrative agent, increased a loan with $36.6 million of outstanding debt by $140.7 million, according to public mortgage documents. Completion is slated for the summer of 2028. In August, the Miami-based developer began demolishing an office building at 6000 North Military Trail, just north of Yamato Road, adjacent to the Old Course at Broken Sound private golf course. Last year, Related Group purchased the asset, which sits on a 8.3-acre parcel, for $50 million from BH Group and PEBB Enterprises, though documents suggest the sellers have retained stakes in the residential project. The joint venture bought the 28-acre office campus for $104 million in 2023 from Office Depot’s parent company ODP, with plans to redevelop it into a mixed-use development. About 405,000 square feet of office space across two buildings will remain, while four new retail and restaurant buildings that together total nearly 43,000 square feet will be added. Luxury gym chain Equinox is expected to open a 37,000-square-foot location, while law firm Kanner & Pintaluga has taken nearly 78,000 square feet. ODP has retained a presence on the campus, having signed a 214,684-square-foot agreement in 2024. A representative for Related Group has yet to provide comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Group secures $177.3M construction financing from Wells Fargo for Boca Raton.
494 luxury apartments + 50 workforce housing units on former Office Depot HQ site.
Related purchased 8.3-acre parcel for $50M in 2024; completion targeted summer 2028.
stories.summary: Related Group closed $177.3 million in construction financing from Wells Fargo for a mixed-income residential development at the former Office Depot headquarters in Boca Raton, Florida. The project includes 494 luxury apartments and 50 workforce housing units on an 8.3-acre site acquired for $50 million. Completion is targeted for summer 2028. The bank increased an existing loan by $140.7 million.
stories.impact: Demonstrates adaptive re-use opportunity and capital availability for South Florida multifamily development. Office-to-residential conversions signal softness in suburban office demand and willingness of lenders to finance alternative uses. For Boca Raton, the 544-unit supply addition will test absorption and rent trajectory in the South Florida market; workforce housing component may face feasibility pressure if rents remain high relative to area AMI.

stories.title: Stabilizing Footprints, Demand Shifts Drive U.S. Office Leasing to 62M SF in Q3
stories.excerpt: U.S. office leasing was on the rise in the third quarter of 2026, as tenant footprints stabilized and competitive employers sought high-quality office space amid dwindling supply. Office leasing volume nationwide totaled 62 million square feet in the third quarter, according to Newmark, in an 18 percent year-over-year uptick that was still 21 percent below pre-pandemic quarterly averages. Newmark’s quarterly report tracks leases spanning 10,000 square feet or more across 62 U.S. markets. July through September marked the country’s sixth consecutive quarter of positive net office absorption, according to the report. The trend outpaces a 15-year low in the office construction pipeline, according to Newmark’s Jessica Morin, head of national occupier research. A majority of pre-pandemic leases have now expired in gateway markets, according to the report, suggesting that the dust is starting to settle around hybrid work shake-ups and return-to-office mandates. An estimated 42 percent of pre-pandemic leases remain in place, with exposure at its highest in Chicago, at 53 percent, and New York City, at 50 percent. “People are cutting by less space than they did earlier in the pandemic, where you saw people slash their portfolio and their square footage by 30 to 40 percent,” Morin said. “Now it’s looking closer to like 10 to 20 percent. Every year going forward, you’re going to see less and less leases that haven’t had a chance yet to adjust for hybrid work.” Those hybrid offices still need desks for employees, Morin said, and companies are eager to retain employees by providing quality office spaces. As old leases expire and pandemic-era downsizing slows, some office tenants are trading up in an increasingly competitive market. The trend has led to more stability in office occupancy, according to the report, despite flat employment numbers among office users. bullets: U.S. office leasing Q3 2026: 62M SF, +18% YoY; sixth consecutive quarter positive absorption.
Volume still 21% below pre-pandemic quarterly average; office construction pipeline at 15-year low.
42% of pre-pandemic leases remain; expiration wave in gateways suggests stabilization ahead.
stories.summary: U.S. office leasing volume totaled 62 million square feet in Q3 2026, marking an 18% year-over-year increase and the sixth consecutive quarter of positive net absorption, according to Newmark. Despite the improvement, leasing remains 21% below pre-pandemic quarterly averages. The office construction pipeline is at a 15-year low, with 42% of pre-pandemic leases still outstanding in gateway markets, suggesting the market is stabilizing post-hybrid work disruption.
stories.impact: Stabilizing office markets reduce downside tail risk for urban multifamily in gateway metros (NYC, SF, DC, Boston), as office anchor tenancy recovers and supports worker demand for nearby housing. However, office supply constraints and tenant footprint stabilization (vs. growth) suggest measured, not explosive, employment growth in these metros. Multifamily developers should expect steady, not booming, rental demand in office-heavy submarkets through 2027.

stories.title: Peachtree Recaps Portland-Area Hotels With $41M Loan
stories.excerpt: Hospitality investment firm WalshDupart has sealed $40.5 million of bridge debt for the recapitalization of two adjacent Hilton-branded hotels in the Portland, Ore., metropolitan area, Commercial Observer has learned. Peachtree Group originated the three-year loan with two 12-month extension options for the 165-room Embassy Suites by Hilton Portland Hillsboro and the 106-room Hampton Inn & Suites Portland/Hillsboro-Evergreen Park in Hillsboro, Ore. Keegan Bisch, vice president of originations and credit at Peachtree, said both hotels have strong demand drivers, being located within Oregon’s Silicon Forest technology hub anchored by Intel and ASML along with a new minor league baseball stadium for the Hillsboro Hops that debuted in April. He noted that the market continues to attract major corporate investments including an advanced semiconductor manufacturing initiative from Intel and a $750 million expansion from biotech firm Genentech. “There is a lot of growth in tech and related industries out there,” Bisch told CO. “There’s very little new supply coming up out there and these are really well located and probably two of the nicest hotels in the market.” Bisch noted that both hotels draw strong business travel, especially the Embassy Suites, which has close to 5,000 square feet of meeting space. Located at 9355-9399 Northeast Tanasbourne Drive 11 miles west of Downtown Portland, the Embassy Suites and Hampton Inn & Suites were developed by Western States Lodging & Management in 2014 as a dual-branded property. WalshDupart acquired the hotels in 2023 and underwent a capital improvement plan. WalshDupart did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: WalshDupart closes $40.5M bridge loan from Peachtree Group for two Hilton hotels.
Embassy Suites (165 rm) + Hampton Inn (106 rm) in Hillsboro, Ore.; 3-yr term + 2x 12-mo ext.
Hillsboro: Intel, ASML, new Hops stadium, Genentech $750M biotech expansion drive demand.
stories.summary: WalshDupart recapitalized two adjacent Hilton-branded hotels in Hillsboro, Oregon with a $40.5 million three-year bridge loan from Peachtree Group. The Embassy Suites (165 rooms) and Hampton Inn (106 rooms) benefit from demand drivers including Intel and ASML, a new minor-league baseball stadium, and Genentech's $750 million biotech expansion in the region.
stories.impact: Signals strong demand tailwinds for the Portland-metro area, particularly the Silicon Forest tech hub around Hillsboro. Major employer capex and facility expansions (Intel, Genentech) typically precede multifamily in-migration and rental demand. Multifamily developers should monitor Hillsboro and surrounding East Metro Portland for land/development opportunities; population and job growth from advanced semiconductor and biotech clusters will support housing demand 12–24 months out.

stories.title: Oxford Properties Buys Six-Property Industrial Portfolio in Phoenix
stories.excerpt: Oxford Properties Group has purchased six industrial properties across three addresses in Phoenix and Tempe, Ariz., near Sky Harbor International Airport. Oxford announced the acquisition of 440 West Fairmont Drive, 800 West Fairmont Drive and 2115 South 11th Avenue, but declined to name the seller or provide the sales price. A source with knowledge of the deal said the 460,000-square-foot light industrial portfolio traded for approximately $100 million. The properties are known as the Sycamore Portfolio and were marketed by a Cushman & Wakefield team of Will Strong, Molly Miller, Jack Stamets, Michael Matchett and Madeline Warren. Revere CRE data, which listed the brokers, and a CBRE brochure indicate that Link Logistics is the seller. “Industrial remains a critical part of Oxford’s U.S. platform and a high-conviction theme for us as we continue to strengthen our vertically integrated operating capabilities in light industrial,” Ankit Bhatt, head of U.S. investments at Oxford Properties, said in a statement. “Our ability to actively recycle capital in this sector allows us to remain responsive to changing market conditions, transact at scale through cycles, and point investment dollars toward highly functional, income-generating assets where we see the strongest relative value.” Oxford’s industrial presence in Phoenix now covers 15 assets and approximately 1.2 million square feet, according to the firm. In 2026, Oxford sold $400 million in properties within its portfolio while investing an equal amount in acquisitions and development, which this transaction is a part of. “Sycamore adds durable income to our portfolio in regional submarkets where we already have a meaningful presence,” Bhatt added. “It also gives our boots-on-the-ground teams an opportunity to leverage their operational expertise to further enhance the performance of these assets over time.” Link Logistics and C&W did not immediately respond to requests for comment. bullets: Oxford Properties purchases Sycamore Portfolio: 460,000 SF, six light industrial properties.
Phoenix/Tempe addresses near Sky Harbor International Airport; ~$100M acquisition price.

stories.summary: Oxford Properties Group acquired a six-property light industrial portfolio spanning approximately 460,000 square feet across Phoenix and Tempe, Arizona, near Sky Harbor International Airport, for roughly $100 million. The portfolio, known as the Sycamore Portfolio, was sold by Link Logistics and includes properties at three addresses. Cushman & Wakefield brokered the transaction.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Industrial acquisitions near Sky Harbor signal strong logistics and supply-chain activity in the Phoenix metro but do not compete for residential land or capital in high-density submarkets. However, industrial growth near airports correlates with job creation (logistics, distribution, warehousing), which typically supports regional multifamily demand 12–18 months downstream. Monitor Phoenix metro employment and wage growth linked to industrial expansion for future multifamily rent-growth signals.
